**Observations:**

- **Dead border pixels sit at initialization scale.** Row 0 (inputs 0–11, 16–27), columns 0–1 of most rows, the last 3–4 pixels of rows 26–27, and all four corners have weights uniformly inside ±0.036 — exactly PyTorch's default U(−1/√784, +1/√784) range, with no sign of shrinkage (so no weight decay) and no sign of tampering. No corner/edge patch has elevated weights into any unit, i.e. no "trigger"-style weights where the data is always zero.
- **Active region is rows 1–27, cols 2–26**, with weak training at row 0 cols 12–15 and col 27 rows 4–20. That footprint (plus the bottom/right edges being more active than top/left) is what one expects from Fashion‑MNIST‑style images, not from centred MNIST digits — consistent with "its dataset".
- **W1 columns are smooth, spatially coherent templates**: e.g. unit 0 negative on the shoulders (rows 1–3, cols 6–11, ≈−0.2 to −0.33) and on rows 12–18 left‑centre (down to −0.558 at input 360), positive at rows 9–11; unit 1 positive across the top (up to 0.484 at input 75); unit 4 a positive vertical stripe at cols 13–15, rows 10–17 (0.17–0.41); units 5/8 a positive/negative pair on the hem rows 25–27 (0.50/−0.47 at input 742); unit 13 a blob at rows 10–13, cols 16–22 (max 0.541 at input 331). Every large value (max |w| ≈ 0.57) is matched by similar values in its row/column neighbours; I found no isolated spikes, no masked‑out interior block, no dead unit, and no duplicated or exactly negated unit (units 1/12 are correlated but clearly distinct).
- **W2** entries lie in ±1.12 with mixed signs in every row and column, roughly balanced sign counts, similar row norms, and no unit dedicated to a single class. Biases (b1 from −0.31 to 0.49, b2 from −0.42 to 0.26) are moderate and plausible.

**Unusual:** no

**What:** nothing

**Confidence:** 15%
